title: Colombo National Museum panels: Vedda religion, livelihood and social change
author_or_institution: Colombo National Museum / Department of National Museums, Sri Lanka
scope: Museum synthesis of Vedda religion, livelihood, social organization and cultural change
limitations: Public museum synthesis; causal wording and typological language require independent corroboration.

title: Legal Personhood and Rights of Nature: Bridging Relational Vedda Worldviews and Sri Lankan Law
author_or_institution: Asanka Edirisinghe and Sandie Suchet-Pearson / Cambridge University Press, Transnational Environmental Law
scope: Vedda indigeneity, language observations, Maduru Oya National Park, Mahaweli resettlement and restrictions on ancestral-land use
limitations: Dambana-focused fieldwork; do not homogenize all Vedda sub-communities.

title: Population histories of the Indigenous Adivasi and Sinhalese from Sri Lanka using whole genomes
author_or_institution: Urban Aragon et al. / Current Biology
scope: Adivasi population history, ancient hunter-gatherer ancestry, effective population size, founder events and consistency with relocation/habitat fragmentation
limitations: Two sampled Adivasi clans; genetics cannot establish a simple unbroken cultural descent from a named prehistoric skeletal population.

title: Reconsidering the Vaddas of Sri Lanka: Biological and cultural continuity, and misconceptions
author_or_institution: Wijerathne Bohingamuwa, Kalangi Rodrigo and Harendralal Namalgamuwa / Quaternary Environments and Humans
scope: Vedda origins, terminology, clan diversity, archaeological sampling and continuity misconceptions
limitations: Use especially to bound direct-prehistoric-continuity and homogeneous-identity claims.

title: Present sociocultural status of the Sri Lankan indigenous people (the Veddas) and future challenges
author_or_institution: Academic chapter in Indigenous People and Nature / Elsevier
scope: Development projects, resettlement, cultural change, assimilation and marginalization
limitations: Broad synthesis; do not use its prehistoric-affinity wording alone to close direct-descent claims.

title: Cultural Borrowing and Religious Transformation: Yakkure and Henanigala Vedda Syncretism with Buddhism
author_or_institution: D. T. H. Ananda and C. A. D. Nahallage / University of Sri Jayewardenepura, Vidyodaya Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences
scope: Yakkure and Henanigala resettlement, Na Yakku traditions, Buddhist/Hindu borrowing, identity and cultural change
limitations: Two-community case study; distinguish documented erosion/adaptation from total cultural disappearance.
